nodes.label: FastAPI ML Service
nodes.rationale: Rule-based early-warning engine (primary) plus an experimental delay estimator (secondary) behind a FastAPI service the Node backend calls. Endpoints: /health (open), /predict, /evaluate-rules, /recommendations, /model-info, /feature-mapping.

nodes.label: ML Service API Key Requirement
nodes.rationale: All endpoints except /health require X-API-Key, and ENVIRONMENT=production without ML_SERVICE_API_KEY refuses to start - an unauthenticated ML endpoint on a network is an open risk-scoring oracle. /health stays open so an orchestrator can probe it.

nodes.label: BASELINE_MEDIAN Prediction
nodes.rationale: No trained model beat a median baseline: median_baseline MAE 306.8 vs random_forest 323.6 and ridge 332.3, every R-squared negative, meaning the models explain less variance than a horizontal line. So the service reports the median, labels it BASELINE_MEDIAN, sets confidence LOW, and says in the response that it is not a model prediction.

nodes.label: Dataset Degeneracy (130 Rows, 22 Vectors)
nodes.rationale: 108 of 130 rows (83%) share one identical feature vector while their real delays span 12 to 2070 days, so for most of the data the model has no information to distinguish rows and the best any algorithm can do is emit the median. All 22 predictor columns are imputed or derived for every row. This is not a tuning failure and no hyperparameter search fixes it.

nodes.label: Grouped Cross-Validation
nodes.rationale: Ordinary K-fold puts copies of the same feature vector in both train and test, so a model that memorised 'this vector to the median of its training rows' scores well without generalising. GroupKFold over identical feature vectors prevents that; it makes the reported numbers worse, which is the point.

nodes.label: ML Service Leakage Boundary
nodes.rationale: The service never queries a database - it holds no credentials and receives the snapshot in the request body, so it cannot reach actual_outcomes even in principle. FeatureSnapshot uses extra='forbid' so a payload carrying actual_delay_days is rejected with 422 at the edge rather than quietly ignored. Training applies the same boundary: audit_dataset.py classifies seven columns as leakage and train.py refuses to run if any reaches the feature matrix.

nodes.label: Feature Mapper
nodes.rationale: The inherited risk_rules.py reads 47 project fields while the deployed snapshot has 21 and exactly one name matches. The mismatch is a difference in kind, not naming: the rules want counts and percentages where the snapshot records booleans, and turning encroachment=true into unauthorized_occupation_cases=5 would be inventing a measurement. So app/services/feature_mapper.py maps 9 DIRECT and 11 DERIVED and marks 24 UNAVAILABLE; rules whose inputs are unavailable are skipped and reported, never evaluated against a guess.

nodes.label: Assessment Sufficiency Check
nodes.rationale: Skipping rules deflates the score, so a project with nothing recorded would otherwise read as low-risk - the opposite of the truth. Raw rule coverage is a poor guard because 10 of 15 rules read NOT NULL booleans that evaluate happily against false and push coverage to 67%; an early version passed its sufficiency check on an entirely empty project for that reason. Sufficiency therefore also requires the core graded measurements, otherwise the response carries sufficient: false and missing_core_inputs.

nodes.label: Rule Engine
nodes.rationale: 15 rules across 13 categories (land progress, compensation, litigation, ownership disputes, land records, R&R, RoW, encroachment, forest clearance, possession, administrative delay, timeline, displacement scale). Every triggered rule returns its evidence - the field values that fired it - so a reader can check the finding rather than trust it.

nodes.label: banded_rule Mutual Exclusivity
nodes.rationale: Severity bands within a rule are mutually exclusive so a project at 15% acquisition is penalised once, not once each for <75, <50 and <25 - enforced structurally by banded_rule rather than by discipline.

nodes.label: Risk Score Formula
nodes.rationale: 15 base plus the sum of contributions, capped at 95. The base reflects that an acquisition with nothing recorded is unassessed rather than risk-free; the cap leaves room for the unmeasured.
